items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Walter Johnson was in the band. He had left Fletcher Henderson’s band. Big Sid Catlett taken his place.

ctx.x: Yeah, down to according to how you at. If you ask, “Bring it up,” and he’ll bring it up. But it went from [? (inaudible)] playing one level of tempo, it went to bring it up and going down. Walter Johnson could do that. It’s like you’re riding a horse, and it’s beautiful. So, Walter Johnson was in the band. He had left Fletcher Henderson’s band. Big Sid Catlett taken his place. It was about money or something. But he’s the one who revolutionized from all them hitting them big cymbals like this. Zildjian came in…
